html:
The French Territory of the Afars and the Issas was the name given to French Somaliland after a referendum in March 1967 in which voters chose to stay under French rule.

Protests for independence had greeted de Gaulle's visit in 1966. Many Somali Issa were kept off the rolls or expelled, while the Afar mostly voted to stay, and the result was widely seen as rigged. The new name stressed the two peoples, and France favoured Afar leaders.

As Somalia and Ethiopia both claimed the territory, France at last agreed to leave. A second referendum in 1977 voted overwhelmingly for independence, and Hassan Gouled Aptidon, an Issa, became the first president of Djibouti.
sum: The French Territory of the Afars and the Issas was the name given to French Somaliland after a referendum in March 1967 in which voters chose to stay under French rule.
